result:
Full check passes across all 20,160 sampled frames. `frame()` worst case 0.83ms (well under the ~2ms requirement), bus budget never exceeded, 2.1 years to 50% wear at full contrast on the hottest pixel — reasonable for a design this animated, and the `orbit()` burn-in walk is already active.

The `automaton-opus5` load failure is a sibling placeholder being worked by a different agent — not mine touch, and `check.mjs` correctly skips it without affecting my design's result.

All required renders are in place:
- `out/automaton-sonnet5.png` — the idle still
- `out/automaton-sonnet5-turn.png` — minute-turn sheet across 10:09:58
- `out/automaton-sonnet5-hour.png` — hour-turn sheet across 10:59:58
- `out/automaton-sonnet5.gif` — minute-turn animation
- `out/automaton-sonnet5-hour.gif` — hour-turn animation
- `out/automaton-sonnet5-wear.png` — burn-in wear map

**Report**

**Idea:** Wire-Bender — a clockwork figure stands at a workbench and bends one continuous steel wire into each digit with its own pliers hands; the hour's finished digit-pairs hang on hooks on a plaque above, touched only once an hour, while the minute pair gets rebuilt — unbent straight, then bent into the new numeral — every sixty seconds, with a flywheel and a toothed escapement anchor ticking away in the corners as the only things that never stop.

**Renders:** `out/automaton-sonnet5.png`, `out/automaton-sonnet5-turn.png`, `out/automaton-sonnet5-hour.png`, `out/automaton-sonnet5.gif`, `out/automaton-sonnet5-hour.gif`, wear map at `out/automaton-sonnet5-wear.png`.

**check.mjs:** PASS, full run (20,160 frames) — worst frame 0.83ms, 0 frames over bus budget, hottest pixel ~2.1 years to 50% wear at full contrast.

**Weakest point:** at the top of the hour, the minute turn and hour turn can coincide (both happen at :00 of a new hour), and for about a second the figure's arms stretch straight up toward the bench's upper reach right as the hour plaque's hooks sit empty mid-swap above it — visually it reads as a dramatic "strongman" pose most of the time, but in one narrow sub-second window the empty hooks and the stretched arms sit close enough to look momentarily cluttered rather than clearly staged. It's rare (once an hour, under a second) and not a correctness bug — the time is never wrong — but it's the one moment I'd keep refining if iterating further.
